title: Safety, Tolerability and Antiviral Activity of GST ‐ HG131 in Chronic Hepatitis B: A Randomized, Double‐Blind Phase IIa Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template—covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)—and the need for lifelong treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST-HG131 in 45 CHB patients. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN.
analysis.methods: The study assessed the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy. Cohorts 1 and 2 (n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 (n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks.
analysis.main_results: At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were −0.65 log10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28-day group and −0.53 log10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28-day group. The 30 mg BID 12-week group showed a greater reduction of −0.89 log10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that GST-HG131, a first-in-class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, significantly reduced HBsAg levels in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the potential of GST-HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB. They may inform future studies on HBV treatment and contribute to the development of more effective therapies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a small sample size and short treatment duration. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a Phase IIa trial with no long-term follow-up data.

analysis.summary_en: This Phase IIa study evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) receiving nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy. The study found that HBsAg reductions were significant in the 30 mg BID 28-day and 12-week groups, with the 12-week group showing the greatest antiviral activity. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg levels below 100 IU/mL. The drug was well tolerated with no dose-related toxicity. However, the study had a small sample size and short treatment duration, limiting the strength of the evidence. These results suggest that GST-HG131 may be a promising candidate for further clinical development as part of functional cure strategies for CHB.

title: Global Underutilization of Antiviral Therapy and Survival Outcomes in Hepatitis B Virus‐Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of 78 Studies and 68,243 Patients

analysis.scope_and_question: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis.

analysis.summary_en: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines. Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed. Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC. These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC. In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis.

title: Hepatitis B and C Virus Among Prisoners in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: ObjectiveTo estimate the pooled prevalence and identify transmission drivers of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections among incarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following a search encompassing Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms from database inception through February 2025. Data were synthesized from 26 studies involving 77,760 prisoners across sub-Saharan Africa. A random-effects model was used to calculate pooled prevalence estimates, assess regional variation, and evaluate odds ratios (OR) for potential transmission risk factors.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The overall pooled prevalence was 13.0% for HBV and 8.0% for HCV among prisoners. Significant regional disparities were observed, with West Africa presenting the highest HBV burden (16.3%) and East Africa showing the highest HCV burden (8.8%). Key independent predictors of infection included sharing sharp objects (OR, 1.98), tattooing (OR, 1.92), and intravenous drug use (OR, 1.38).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report specific controversies or evidence gaps related to the primary target entity, hepatitis B virus.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Addressing these gaps requires targeted screening, comprehensive harm reduction, condom provision, and integrating prison health services into national elimination strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence and identify transmission drivers of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections among incarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa. The evidence base included 26 studies with 77,760 prisoners, and a random-effects model was used to calculate pooled prevalence and assess risk factors. The overall pooled prevalence was 13.0% for HBV and 8.0% for HCV, with significant regional disparities observed. West Africa had the highest HBV burden (16.3%), while East Africa had the highest HCV burden (8.8%). Key risk factors included sharing sharp objects, tattooing, and intravenous drug use. The review highlights the need for targeted screening, harm reduction, and integration of prison health services into national strategies to address the high burden of viral hepatitis in this population.

title: Evaluating the potential of treatment options for chronic hepatitis B

analysis.scope_and_question: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide, but long-term or even lifelong viral suppression with nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) seldom clears hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), so-called 'functional cure.' In recent years, a shift in treatment strategy from viral suppression toward cure has emerged, catalyzed by three revised international hepatitis B guidelines (2025-2026) and the first-in-class phase 3 evidence that a finite antiviral therapy, the antisense oligonucleotide bepirovirsen, can achieve a functional cure in about one in five NA-suppressed CHB patients with baseline HBsAg below 3000 IU/mL.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: AREAS COVERED: We evaluated the spectrum of established and emerging treatment options for CHB, organized around quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) as the axis for selecting and sequencing therapy.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Coverage spans backbone NAs and pegylated interferon-α, an HBsAg-guided roadmap, finite NA therapy and off-treatment outcomes, bepirovirsen, other virus-targeting and immunomodulatory agents, and genome-directed covalently closed circular DNA silencing and editing.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: EXPERT OPINION: Bepirovirsen's approaching approval is an inflection point.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: qHBsAg should guide personalized, sequential therapy, with partial cure (HBsAg < 100 IU/mL) as a potential intermediate target when functional cure is unlikely.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates treatment options for chronic hepatitis B, focusing on the shift from viral suppression to cure, with bepirovirsen as a promising new therapy. The review covers backbone NAs, pegylated interferon-α, HBsAg-guided therapy, finite NA therapy, and other emerging treatments.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The weighted prevalence of HBV infection with ≥F2 fibrosis was 0.63% (95% CI 0.52% to 0.77%), corresponding to approximately 6.08 million individuals in China. The weighted prevalence of HCV infection with ≥F2 fibrosis was 0.05% (95% CI 0.03% to 0.08%), corresponding to about 0.48 million individuals. The prevalence of liver steatosis was 1.82% (95% CI 1.56% to 2.13%) for HBV and 0.06% (95% CI 0.04% to 0.10%) for HCV, representing roughly 17.30 million and 0.61 million individuals respectively. Diagnosis rates were 59.78% for HBV and 38.02% for HCV, with treatment rates of 7.60% and 48.66% respectively.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report any controversies, methodological weaknesses, or specific evidence gaps concerning the prevalence of HBV or HCV with liver fibrosis or steatosis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Implement proactive case‐finding and strengthen linkage to care to improve diagnosis and treatment, supporting national elimination of viral hepatitis.

analysis.summary_en: Using data from the 2020 National Serological Survey of Viral Hepatitis in China, this population‐based study estimated the prevalence of HBV and HCV infection coexisting with liver fibrosis (stage ≥F2) and steatosis among 69,351 adults aged 15–69 years. Among 4,236 HBV‐positive and 122 HCV‐positive participants, the weighted prevalence of advanced fibrosis was 0.63% (95% CI 0.52%–0.77%) for HBV and 0.05% (95% CI 0.03%–0.08%) for HCV, representing roughly 6.08 million and 0.48 million people, respectively. Liver steatosis was present in 1.82% (95% CI 1.56%–2.13%) of HBV‐infected and 0.06% (95% CI 0.04%–0.10%) of HCV‐infected individuals, corresponding to about 17.30 million and 0.61 million persons. Diagnosis rates were 59.8% for HBV and 38.0% for HCV, with treatment rates of 7.6% and 48.7%, respectively. The authors conclude that China faces a substantial burden of advanced liver disease among those with viral hepatitis, underscoring the urgent need for proactive case‐finding and improved linkage to care to achieve hepatitis elimination.

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Hepatitis B and/or C Virus Infections among Medical Waste Handlers in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Health systems around the world are severely impacted by hepatitis B Virus and hepatitis C Virus, particularly in low- and middle-income nations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A5 A6 A7 A8 A9 A10 A11 A12.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: This study found that having multiple sexual partners and prior exposure to sharp objects were associated with Hepatitis B Virus and/or Hepatitis C Virus infection among medical waste handlers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Significant heterogeneity is shown in the Galbraith plot, with I 2 = 96.21% ( p < 0.001).
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Therefore, reducing infection risk requires promoting safe sexual practices and strengthening infection prevention and control measures in healthcare settings.

analysis.summary_en: This review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the prevalence of hepatitis B and/or C among Ethiopian medical waste handlers, finding a pooled prevalence of 13% (95% CI: 5-21%). Significant heterogeneity was noted, with behavioral and occupational factors identified as risk factors.

title: Superior Efficacy of Besifovir in Reducing Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Compared to Tenofovir in Chronic Hepatitis B Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.

analysis.scope_and_question: Besifovir dipivoxil maleate (BSV) is a novel therapeutic option for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service database from 2018 to 2022.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: In the overall population, 57 cases of HCC were reported in the BSV group (2,358 individuals, 5,918 person-years), while 1,268 cases of HCC were reported in the TDF group (30,025 individuals, 83,587 person-years).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Propensity score matching was conducted at a 1:3 ratio to minimize selection bias.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: BSV treatment demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing the risk of HCC compared to TDF, regardless of baseline cirrhosis status.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared the efficacy of besifovir (BSV) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in reducing hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk among chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. BSV showed a significantly lower incidence of HCC (1.59 times lower) compared to TDF, consistent across cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic subgroups.

title: Circulation and recombination-driven diversity of duck hepatitis B virus in domesticated geese in Guangdong, southern China

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the circulation and recombination-driven diversity of duck hepatitis B virus (DHBV) in domesticated geese in Guangdong, southern China, as DHBV is a valuable comparative model for human hepatitis B virus (HBV) due to its shared genomic organization and reverse transcription-based replication, despite having only ∼40% nucleotide identity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 901 deceased domesticated geese liver samples collected from five regions in Guangdong province, southern China, to assess the prevalence and genetic diversity of DHBV.
analysis.methods: Nested PCR screening was used to detect DHBV infection, revealing an overall infection prevalence of 34.1% (307/901). Amino acid analysis of the preS domain of the large envelope protein and genetic characterization of 44 complete genomes were conducted to evaluate variability and circulation patterns.
analysis.main_results: Amino acid analysis of the preS domain showed extensive variability, including the G133E mutation in 47.7% (21/44) of strains and genotype-associated substitutions at residues 117 and 120. Genetic characterization revealed exclusive circulation of genotypes I and II (DHBV-I and DHBV-II), with no detection of the Western-associated DHBV-III. Twenty recombination events were identified, six of which involved the study sequences as parental strains.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the ongoing circulation and evolutionary complexity of DHBV in southern China, emphasizing the role of active recombination among co-circulating strains in driving viral heterogeneity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results underscore the need for longitudinal genomic surveillance to detect emerging DHBV variants and inform strategies for monitoring and managing the virus in domesticated geese populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which may not capture the full dynamics of DHBV circulation over time. The evidence is moderate, based on prevalence and genetic analysis of a single geographic region.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the circulation and recombination-driven diversity of duck hepatitis B virus (DHBV) in domesticated geese in Guangdong, southern China. It analyzed 901 liver samples and found an overall infection prevalence of 34.1%. Amino acid analysis of the preS domain revealed extensive variability, including the G133E mutation in 47.7% of strains. Genetic characterization of 44 complete genomes showed exclusive circulation of genotypes I and II, with no detection of DHBV-III. Twenty recombination events were identified, six involving the study sequences as parental strains. These findings highlight the evolutionary complexity of DHBV in the region and the importance of genomic surveillance to monitor emerging variants. The study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to capture long-term circulation dynamics, and the evidence is moderate due to the focus on a single geographic area.

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of reliable methods for predicting individual treatment response in chronic hepatitis B patients, as long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in some individuals but not others.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This opinion review discusses the application of machine learning in predicting treatment response for chronic hepatitis B, focusing on the potential of ML to complement existing clinical tools.
analysis.methods: The authors review the use of machine learning in three areas: quantitative image analysis, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights early but encouraging results from machine learning applications in predicting fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, particularly through the integration of clinical and pathological data.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that machine learning can enhance existing tools for assessing treatment response in chronic hepatitis B, offering a novel approach to personalized prediction without replacing current methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that machine learning could improve the precision of predicting which patients with chronic hepatitis B are likely to achieve fibrosis reversal, aiding in more tailored treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the fact that most current models are based on small, single-center retrospective cohorts, which may affect their generalizability and require further prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of machine learning to address the challenge of predicting individual responses to antiviral therapy in chronic hepatitis B patients. The authors highlight three promising areas: image-based quantitative analysis, integration of clinical and pathological data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction based on serial measurements. They emphasize that while ML shows early promise, its clinical adoption requires validation across larger, multi-center studies and improved model interpretability. The study underscores the importance of using ML to complement existing tools rather than replace them, offering a novel approach to personalized treatment strategies. However, the evidence is limited by the reliance on small, single-center datasets, which may restrict the generalizability of findings. The implications of this work suggest that ML could enhance the precision of predicting fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, contributing to more effective and individualized care.

title: The long noncoding RNA MAPKAPK5-AS1 promotes the formation of hepatitis B virus cccDNA by modulating the expression of NABP1

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the role of host long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in the hepatitis B virus (HBV) life cycle, addressing the need to understand the mechanisms underlying HBV infection and cccDNA formation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A loss-of-function screen targeting 1779 human lncRNAs was conducted to identify host factors involved in HBV infection, focusing on the HBV life cycle in human cells.
analysis.methods: The study employed a loss-of-function screen to identify lncRNAs associated with HBV infection, followed by mechanistic experiments to elucidate the role of a specific lncRNA, lnc-MAAS, in cccDNA formation.
analysis.main_results: The study identified lnc-MAAS as a host factor required for HBV infection and found that it affects cccDNA formation by modulating the expression of NABP1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that lnc-MAAS plays a crucial role in HBV cccDNA formation through the regulation of NABP1 expression, providing new insights into the mechanisms of HBV infection and potentially contributing to the development of novel anti-HBV therapeutics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study’s findings could inform the development of novel anti-HBV therapeutics by targeting lnc-MAAS and NABP1, which may help in the management of chronic hepatitis B and related complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s limitations include the use of a loss-of-function screen, which may not fully capture the complexity of the HBV life cycle, and the need for further validation of the findings in clinical settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified lnc-MAAS as a host factor required for HBV infection and found that it modulates NABP1 expression to affect cccDNA formation, providing new insights for potential anti-HBV therapeutics.

title: Effect of Hepatitis B virus X T118N mutant protein in HepG2 cell cycle and apoptosis regulation

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to examine the effect of HBx T118N mutant on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in HepG2 cells, addressing the need to understand the role of this specific HBV mutation in liver disease development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used HepG2 cells and analyzed the effect of HBx T118N mutant protein on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation through gene expression analysis and flow cytometry.
analysis.methods: The study employed RT-qPCR to analyze CyclinE, p21, Bax, and Bcl-2 gene expression, and flow cytometry with PI and Annexin V-PI staining to assess cell cycle and apoptosis. Caspase 3 activity was also measured using a colorimetric assay.
analysis.main_results: HBx T118N mutant increased CyclinE expression and Bax and Bcl-2 mRNA levels in HepG2 cells, and caused an increase in AnnexinV+/PI- and AnnexinV+/PI+ cell populations compared to HBx wild-type expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The data suggest that HBx T118N influences cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in a manner slightly different from HBx K130M/V131I, indicating potential differences in the mechanisms of liver disease development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the role of HBx T118N in liver disease and suggest the need for further investigations to understand its involvement in chronic liver disease and liver cirrhosis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of a single cell line and the absence of in vivo studies, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined the effect of HBx T118N mutant on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in HepG2 cells, finding increased CyclinE expression and altered Bax and Bcl-2 mRNA levels, suggesting differences in liver disease mechanisms compared to HBx K130M/V131I.

title: Hepatic Steatosis in People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Africa: Prevalence, Correlates, and Clinical Significance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: To address data gaps around metabolic liver disease in Africa, within the Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET), we evaluated participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP).
analysis.study_design_and_population: Using multivariable logistic regression, we identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical associations with SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m), and evaluated whether SLD severity was independently associated with fibrosis.
analysis.methods: Across 6 countries and 1601 participants (age range, 12-80 years; 39.5% female; 4% with diabetes; 11% unhealthy alcohol use; median body mass index, 24.4), 421 (26.3%) had SLD; 219 (13.7%) had severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m).
analysis.main_results: Older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status were associated with SLD. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV status, HBV treatment, and country, severe steatosis, but not mild and moderate forms (i.e., 248-279 dB/m), was associated with a 8.4% (95%, 1.9%-14.9%) increased probability of fibrosis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In conclusion, SLD was common in people with CHB in Africa and its severe form was associated with liver fibrosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These data support screening for metabolic comorbidities as part of HBV care and treatment in Africa.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Over limited follow-up (median 2.69 years) and small number of deaths, SLD was not associated with all-cause or liver-related mortality.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address data gaps on metabolic liver disease in Africa by evaluating participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection for steatotic liver disease using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). The research was conducted across six countries involving 1601 participants, with 421 (26.3%) found to have SLD and 219 (13.7%) with severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). The study identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical factors associated with SLD, including older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status. After adjusting for various factors, severe steatosis was linked to an increased probability of fibrosis. However, SLD was not associated with mortality during limited follow-up. The findings highlight the importance of screening for metabolic comorbidities in HBV care and suggest that severe steatosis may be a marker for fibrosis. The study's limitations include its short follow-up period and small number of deaths, which may affect the strength of conclusions about mortality.

title: Ultrasound findings across liver fibrosis stages defined by transient elastography in patients with chronic hepatitis B in Georgia

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major cause of chronic liver disease and may progress to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to evaluate conventional abdominal ultrasound (US) findings across liver fibrosis stages defined by transient elastography (TE) in patients with CHB.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this cross-sectional study, 232 adults with CHB were included. Conventional abdominal US and TE data were available for 231 patients. Among the 231 patients, 71.9% were classified as F0-F1, 21.6% as F2-F3, and 6.5% as F4.
analysis.methods: US findings were evaluated in relation to liver fibrosis stages defined by TE-derived liver stiffness measurements. Differences in liver stiffness according to US findings were assessed using the independent-samples t-test.
analysis.main_results: Patients with heterogeneous liver echotexture had significantly higher liver stiffness than those with normal liver echotexture (8.71 ± 6.89 vs. 5.65 ± 1.30 kPa; mean difference, 3.06 kPa; 95% CI 1.78-4.34 kPa; p < 0.001). Patients with splenomegaly had significantly higher liver stiffness than those without splenomegaly (17.31 ± 15.18 vs. 6.55 ± 2.82 kPa; mean difference, 10.77 kPa; 95% CI 2.00-19.54 kPa; p = 0.020).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Conventional abdominal US findings, particularly heterogeneous liver echotexture and splenomegaly, were associated with higher liver stiffness in patients with CHB. These findings support the complementary role of conventional abdominal US in the comprehensive non-invasive evaluation of patients with CHB.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the use of conventional abdominal US as a non-invasive tool for assessing liver fibrosis stages in patients with CHB, potentially improving surveillance and early detection of liver disease progression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the reliance on TE-derived liver stiffness measurements. The evidence is moderate as it is based on abstract-only data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between conventional abdominal ultrasound findings and liver fibrosis stages in patients with chronic hepatitis B in Georgia. It highlights that heterogeneous liver echotexture and splenomegaly are linked to higher liver stiffness, as measured by transient elastography. These results suggest that ultrasound can complement non-invasive assessments of liver fibrosis in CHB patients. The study is cross-sectional and based on abstract-only data, which limits the strength of the evidence to moderate. The findings may have implications for improving surveillance and early detection of liver disease progression in CHB patients.

title: Becoming Physically Active and Risks of Mortality and Liver-Related Events in Adults With Chronic Hepatitis B: A Nationwide Cohort Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Physical activity (PA) confers several health benefits; however, whether increasing PA among physically inactive adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is associated with lower risks of adverse clinical outcomes remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We included 318,131 adults with CHB who were physically inactive at the initial health screening (Exam 1) and completed a subsequent screening within 4 years (Exam 2).
analysis.methods: We used the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database.
analysis.main_results: During a median 7.9-year follow-up (IQR, 5.2-9.5), 7609 deaths occurred.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: MVPA initiation was associated with lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), a lower risk of liver-related events (subdistribution HR [subHR], 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and, more modestly, of HCC (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared with those remaining inactive.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide large-scale epidemiological evidence supporting further evaluation of PA promotion in physically inactive patients with CHB.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The association was more pronounced in older adults, women, never smokers, non-drinkers, and untreated participants (all p for interaction ≤ 0.03).

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between initiating moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and reduced risks of mortality and liver-related events in adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Using the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database, the researchers followed 318,131 physically inactive adults with CHB over a median of 7.9 years. They found that MVPA initiation was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), reduced liver-related events (subHR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and a modest decrease in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared to those who remained inactive. The associations were stronger in specific subgroups, including older adults, women, and untreated participants. The study highlights the potential public health significance of promoting physical activity in CHB patients, though it does not provide direct causal evidence.

title: Risk factors for postpartum alanine aminotransferase elevation in women with chronic hepatitis B infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Background Postpartum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevation is common in women with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection and may adversely affect maternal recovery and long-term disease outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines; the registration number is CRD420251208005. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and WanFang databases were searched from their inception to 1 January 2026.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The meta-analysis demonstrated that hepatitis B e-antigen (HBeAg) positivity (odds ratio [OR] = 3.03; 95% CI [1.91–4.81]), higher baseline hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA levels (OR = 1.39; 95% CI [1.04–1.86]), and elevated antepartum ALT levels were significantly associated with postpartum ALT elevation. A subgroup analysis revealed that antepartum ALT elevation, defined as a categorical variable (ALT >1 ULN), showed a strong association with postpartum ALT elevation (OR = 5.54, 95% CI 3.78–8.12), whereas continuous ALT increase showed a smaller effect size. HBeAg positivity, high baseline HBV DNA levels, and elevated antepartum ALT levels are key risk factors for postpartum ALT elevation in women with CHB.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The risk factors associated with postpartum ALT elevation remain inconsistent across studies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Additionally, younger maternal age may confer increased susceptibility.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify risk factors for postpartum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevation in women with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection. The study included 17 cohort studies involving 6,876 women with CHB. Key findings indicated that HBeAg positivity, higher baseline HBV DNA levels, and elevated antepartum ALT levels were significantly associated with postpartum ALT elevation. Subgroup analysis showed that antepartum ALT elevation, defined as ALT >1 ULN, had a strong association with postpartum ALT elevation, while continuous ALT increase showed a smaller effect. Increasing maternal age was associated with a reduced risk of postpartum ALT elevation. The review highlights the importance of monitoring antepartum ALT levels and managing HBeAg positivity and HBV DNA levels in women with CHB during pregnancy and postpartum periods. The findings suggest that younger maternal age may increase susceptibility to postpartum ALT elevation.

title: A comprehensive evaluation on the impact of MASLD on the prognosis of chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma following hepatectomy: results from retrospective multicenter cohort study and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: This study evaluates the impact of MASLD on the prognosis of chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) following hepatectomy. The central question is whether MASLD modifies postoperative outcomes in patients with CHB-HCC.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study combines a retrospective multicenter cohort study with a meta-analysis. It included 424 patients from multiple centers and a meta-analysis involving 6653 patients. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to adjust for confounding factors, and Cox regression analysis was performed to identify independent prognostic factors.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that the MASLD-CHB-HCC group showed significantly better overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared to the CHB-HCC group in the retrospective cohort study. However, after PSM, no significant differences were observed. Subgroup analyses revealed that among non-lean patients, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group had better OS and RFS, particularly in BMI ≥ 23 and BMI ≥ 25 subgroups. The meta-analysis confirmed these findings, indicating that MASLD has differential impacts on survival prognosis in CHB-HCC patients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights conflicting findings between the initial analysis and the PSM-adjusted results, suggesting potential confounding factors. Additionally, the differential effects of MASLD on survival were observed only in non-lean subgroups, indicating a need for further research to understand the mechanisms behind these differences.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on understanding the mechanisms by which MASLD affects survival in CHB-HCC patients, particularly in non-lean subgroups. There is a need for larger, prospective studies to validate these findings and explore the role of BMI in mediating the impact of MASLD on prognosis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of MASLD on the prognosis of chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) following hepatectomy. A retrospective multicenter cohort study and meta-analysis were conducted, involving 424 and 6653 patients, respectively. Initial findings suggested that MASLD-CHB-HCC patients had better overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared to CHB-HCC patients, but these differences disappeared after propensity score matching (PSM). Subgroup analyses revealed that non-lean patients with MASLD-CHB-HCC had significantly improved OS and RFS, particularly in BMI ≥ 23 and ≥ 25 groups. The meta-analysis supported these results, indicating that MASLD has differential effects on survival outcomes in CHB-HCC patients. The study underscores the need for further research to clarify the mechanisms behind these differences and to explore the role of BMI in influencing prognosis.

title: Concomitant Liver Steatosis in Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection Is Linked to a Distinct Cytokine Profile and Reduced Viral Load.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the impact of liver steatosis on antiviral immune responses and viral load in chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, addressing a knowledge gap in the field.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved 66 treatment-naive patients with chronic HBV infection, comparing those with and without liver steatosis.
analysis.methods: Cytokine and chemokine patterns were assessed in plasma samples, along with viral load and aminotransferase levels in blood samples.
analysis.main_results: Patients with HBV infection and liver steatosis had a lower viral load and reduced plasma levels of several cytokines and chemokines, including IL-2, IL-9, IL-15, IL-18, CCL2, CCL4, and CXCL10, as well as reduced aminotransferase levels. Other cytokines did not significantly differ between the groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that liver steatosis in chronic HBV infection is associated with a dampened immune response, which may influence disease progression and HCC risk independently of viral load.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results caution that liver steatosis may alter the immune response in chronic HBV infection, potentially impacting disease outcomes and HCC risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and small sample size, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of liver steatosis on antiviral immune responses and viral load in chronic HBV infection. It found that patients with liver steatosis had lower viral loads and reduced levels of several cytokines, suggesting a dampened immune response that may influence disease progression and HCC risk.

title: Prevalence and determinants of hepatitis B vaccination uptake among pregnant women in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: Despite more than two decades of hepatitis B vaccination implementation across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains hyperendemic in the region, with vertical transmission an important route of infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. DATA SOURCES: Following prospective registration (PROSPERO), we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and Scopus for peer-reviewed studies published up to August 2026, supplemented by African Journals Online and Google Scholar. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR SELECTING STUDIES: Observational studies reporting HBV vaccination uptake among pregnant women in SSA countries were included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled prevalence of HBV vaccination uptake was 18% (95% CI 14% to 21%) with substantial heterogeneity (I2=99.2%) observed. Studies from West Africa (12; n=8062) reported higher vaccine uptake (24%, 95% CI 17% to 31%; p<0.001). Available studies identified socioeconomic, behavioural and healthcare-related factors associated with uptake, though evidence was limited. The overall certainty of evidence was considered very low using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, reflecting serious concerns regarding inconsistency, risk of bias and small-study effects.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence of small-study effects or potential publication bias was observed (Egger’s test, p<0.001).
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Targeted, context-specific interventions to improve awareness, access and integration of vaccination into antenatal care services are needed to enhance uptake. Future research should examine barriers and evaluate interventions to increase vaccination coverage in this priority population.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the prevalence of hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination uptake and identify its determinants among pregnant women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). A total of 21 studies involving 15,804 pregnant women from seven SSA countries were included. The pooled prevalence of HBV vaccination uptake was found to be 18% (95% CI 14% to 21%) with substantial heterogeneity (I2=99.2%). Studies from West Africa reported higher uptake (24%, 95% CI 17% to 31%). Socioeconomic, behavioural, and healthcare-related factors were associated with uptake, though evidence was limited. The certainty of evidence was very low due to inconsistency, risk of bias, and small-study effects. The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve vaccination rates and suggest future research to examine barriers and evaluate interventions.
